newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday new economic policy measures will be announced this week, in a clear message to investors in India to stop worrying about the government's commitment to reforms.
"Some decisions will be coming in the next two to three
days," Deve Gowda told the All India Association of Industries at a meeting in Bombay.
Parliament's approval will be needed for further
measures the government planned to announce in the budget set for February 28, he said.
Investors in India's stock markets anticipated good
news on the way, and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE's) top 30-share index shot up 3.7 percent higher on Monday, gaining 127.12 points to finish at 3,562.74.

** The expert panel on small enterprises mooted highly debatable and sweeping reforms in the small-scale sector to make it globally competitive, the Financial Express reports. The committee recommended abolition of the reservation policy, scrapping foreign equity limit and enhancing investment limit to 30 million rupees for the sector, the paper says.
** The bourse regulator (SEBI) allowed three foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to invest in 100 percent debt funds, the Observer says.
This investment route was approved by the government and
SEBI in December. The clearance was for investments totalling $203 million in the next three months, the paper reports.

** Daewoo Corporation has got clearance from the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to increase its equity stake in joint venture DCM Daewoo Ltd to a maximum 87 percent from 75 percent, the Business Standard reports.
The formal letter of approval is expected in a few days.
The DCM group's equity stake in the company is thus set to go down to about 1.5 percent against a 34 percent stake the Indian partner held when the joint venture was formed, the paper says.
** Germany's Volkswagen AG plans to invest $100 million in a car manufacturing plant in India, the Press Trust of India (PTI) on Monday quoted a senior Volkswagen official as saying.
PTI said Bernd Lohning told the news agency in the
southern city of Bangalore that Volkswagen was seeking an Indian partner and hoped the factory would begin producing two models later this year. PTI did not give Lohning's title.
"We are looking forward to invest to the tune of about
$100 million in India, and the plant would be in Bangalore," PTI quoted Lohning as saying.
MARKETS:
** The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index
gained 23.25 points, or 2.36 percent, to 1,009.15.
** The Delhi index rose 4.9 percent to 761.53 points
** The Calcutta index added 14.58 points to 460.90
** The Madras index was up 68.40 points to 3,361.87
